factors.name: General size and connectivity
factors.summary: A single general factor on which all eight measures load, explaining 76% of the variance. It is carried most strongly by Control flow complexity, Size and Number of duplicate tasks (about 0.99), followed by the connector degrees and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.86–0.96), so larger nets in this dataset also have more choices and parallelism, more duplicate labels and more arcs per node. Density loads negatively (-0.73), as expected because its denominator grows with size, while Separability loads only moderately (0.44, communality 0.19) and is poorly explained.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, overall KMO 0.73). One factor was extracted, in line with the eigenvalues (6.25, then 0.82). It is a general factor: for these 288 nets, size, control-flow complexity, duplicate tasks and connectivity vary together, and density decreases as nets grow. This one-factor result does not separate size from connectivity or concurrency, but with one factor this is expected, so it should not be read as proof that these aspects cannot be told apart.
caveats: Sequentiality and Connector Mismatch were removed by the MSA filter, and Connector Heterogeneity, Token split and Number of empty sequence flows were constant, so aspects such as sequentiality and connector balance are not represented.
Separability has a low communality (0.19) and is largely unexplained by the factor.
Several loadings near 0.995 and very small trailing eigenvalues point to near-redundant measures in this dataset, likely tied to the discovery algorithms that produced the nets.
The result reflects shared variance in this particular set of nets and does not show causal relations among the measures.
